initial_observation.chief_complaint: history of sun sensitivity and development of crusting skin lesions for the past 2 years
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: Typically, after 30 min of direct sun exposure, such as while tending to plants in the garden, he would start to feel burning and excruciating pain in the skin on the face, hands, and even fingertips. He was repeatedly forced to go inside to relieve the skin burning. He also noticed crusting skin lesions appearing on the dorsa of the hands within days after sun exposure.
presenting_symptoms: burning and excruciating pain in the skin on the face, hands, and fingertips after sun exposure
crusting skin lesions on the dorsa of the hands
known_prior_history: myelodysplastic syndrome with multilineage dysplasia (MDS-MLD) diagnosed 6 years ago

evidence_items.source_text: Clinical examination revealed thickened, lichenified skin with one fresh blister, numerous crusts, indented scars, and milia formation on the dorsa of the hands and some on the back of the neck and face (Fig. 1A).

CBC showed anaemia, and reduced thrombocyte and white blood cell count consistent with his MDS. Liver and renal function parameters were normal. There were no detectable autoantibodies associated with connective tissue diseases.
Skin biopsy demonstrated subepidermal blistering with scarce inflammatory reaction, suggesting a porphyria (Fig. 1B).

A plasma fluorescence scan was positive and revealed a massive increase in total porphyrins at 33.9 umol/L (normal < 1.30) and free protoporphyrin 30 umol/L (normal < 0.20). A diagnosis of erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) secondary to MDS was made.

Two years after the diagnosis of acquired EPP, our patient was able to control his photosensitivity with the above-mentioned sun-protective measures and did not require the use of afamelanotide. To date, he has not developed any signs of liver toxicity despite consistently high levels of plasma porphyrins, which are being monitored on regular basis.

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: A diagnosis of erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP) secondary to MDS was made.
accepted_aliases: acquired erythropoietic protoporphyria secondary to myelodysplastic syndrome
